about: Grace Tyler Estate Winery sits on the north shore of Oneida Lake in Constantia, about forty minutes north of Syracuse. Richard and Elizabeth Hamilton bought the property in 2012, planted cold-hardy vines, and waited five years for their first harvest in 2017. The tasting room they opened in 2018 is built from aspen poplar cut on the property, with a bar made from a neighbor’s maple. In 2022 Operation Oswego County honored the couple with its entrepreneur award for drawing visitors to the lake’s north shore.

La Crescent is a grape made for winters like Oswego County’s. It was bred at the University of Minnesota by Peter Hemstad and James Luby, crossed in 1988 from St. Pepin and a hardy hybrid selection, and it survives cold of minus 20 to minus 35°F. It descends partly from Muscat, which gives it its perfume, and it has won more Governor’s Cups at the International Cold Climate Wine Competition than any other variety entered. Its natural acidity keeps it in balance at a touch of sweetness.

The 2025 is made semi-dry. Expect apricot, peach and citrus, with orange blossom and a tropical edge, the classic La Crescent profile. The acidity keeps the sweetness lively, which makes it a natural partner for spice, smoke and the char of a wood fire. It is the same grape as the winery’s skin-fermented La Crescent on this list. Tasting the two side by side shows how much the winemaker’s choices can change a single variety.
facts: 100% La Crescent (cold-hardy hybrid, University of Minnesota)
North shore of Oneida Lake, Oswego County, New York
